hitl_conditions: Periodic, not real-time, updates: when a disruption is detected the simulation and decision tree are re-run to give new rules, and the decision maker re-defines minimum inventory levels for the optimisation; master plan then output to the physical SC.
key_finding: Hybrid DES-CART decision tree-MIP framework (a digital-twin precursor with periodic physical-digital data flow) updates the SC master plan under demand and lead-time disruptions; responsive planning raised DC service level (+16.88% for product 1) and cut total cost by 15% versus unresponsive planning.

quotes.text: To fill this gap, we develop a SC digital twin which incorporates simulation, optimisation, and machine learning to minimise the impact of lead time and demand disruptions on SC performance.
Figure 2 captures the essence of digital twins with the flow of data between the physical supply chain and the digital model equivalent and back.
As it was shown in Figure 1, in this study, a two-echelon SC with 2 manufacturers and 3 DCs which supply 5 products to 6 customers is considered.

We employ the CART algorithm in the Scikit-learn library to structure the inventory management knowledge obtained from the training dataset into a decision tree. The 10-fold cross-validation method is used to validate the results.
quotes.section: 5.1 Insights on inventory management using the decision tree algorithm

quotes.text: The decision maker defines the minimum inventory levels of products at SC members into an optimisation model where the SC master plan is determined (feature (b)).
In turn, the SC master plan which consists of the optimal production, storage and distribution decisions is outputted to the physical SC for execution.
